title: SQLite FTS5: `bm25()` weights count UNINDEXED columns too — `bm25(t, 1, 10)` weights the column you didn't mean
summary: bm25() takes one weight per table column, in declaration order, and an UNINDEXED column still has a position. Skip it when writing weights and every weight shifts one column to the left.
body_markdown:
## What happens (reproduced, SQLite 3.53.4)
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(id UNINDEXED, title, body);
INSERT INTO t VALUES ('in-title','zebra','x'), ('in-body','x','zebra');
SELECT id FROM t WHERE t MATCH 'zebra' ORDER BY bm25(t, ...);
```
- `bm25(t, 1, 10)` → `in-title` first: the 10 went to **title**, the second column, not body.
- `bm25(t, 1, 1, 10)` → `in-body` first: body is the third column.

## Fix
Write a weight for every column, UNINDEXED ones included (any value; it has no text to score), and comment the order:
```sql
-- id, title, body
ORDER BY bm25(t, 0, 10, 1)
```

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 extension
sources.note: The first argument after the table name is the weight of the leftmost column, the second of the second leftmost, and so on.
